def-anchored-finite-metric-graph-h1-spac:
## Definition

Assume the Axiom of Choice as required by the cited one-dimensional
representative interface. A **finite metric graph**
$\Gamma=(V,E,\partial_-,\partial_+,\ell)$ consists of finite vertex and
edge sets $V,E$, endpoint maps $\partial_-,\partial_+:E\to V$, and edge
lengths $0<\ell_e<\infty$. Distinct edges with the same endpoints are
allowed, as are loop edges with $\partial_-e=\partial_+e$. Every vertex is
an endpoint of at least one edge. The two endpoint incidences $(e,-)$ and
$(e,+)$ remain distinct even for a loop. A graph path is a finite sequence
$z_0,e_1,z_1,\ldots,e_n,z_n$ with $n\ge0$ and
$\{\partial_-e_j,\partial_+e_j\}=
\{z_{j-1},z_j\}$ for every $j$; a loop permits $z_{j-1}=z_j$. Vertices in
the same connected edge component are those joined by such a path. Orient
each edge only to choose its coordinate $x_e\in[0,\ell_e]$, with $0$ at
$\partial_-e$ and $\ell_e$ at $\partial_+e$. For $z\in V$, let
$\mathcal I(z):=\{(e,-):\partial_-e=z\}\cup\{(e,+):\partial_+e=z\}$
be its finite set of endpoint incidences.
The edge-product spaces are

$$H:=\bigoplus_{e\in E}L^2(0,\ell_e;\mathbb R),\qquad \mathcal W:=\bigoplus_{e\in E}H^1(0,\ell_e;\mathbb R).$$

For $w_e\in H^1(0,\ell_e)$, its endpoint values mean the values of the unique
absolutely continuous representative supplied by
[[cor-one-dimensional-w-one-p-functions-have-absolutely-continuous-representatives]].
The **trace-matching graph Sobolev space** is the subspace of $\mathcal W$
whose endpoint-incidence traces all agree at each vertex. For a designated
anchor set $D\subseteq V$, define the **anchored graph energy space**

$$V_D:=\{w\in\mathcal W:\ w_{\iota}=w_{\iota'}\text{ whenever }\iota,\iota'\in\mathcal I(v),\quad w_{\iota}=0\text{ for each }v\in D,\ \iota\in\mathcal I(v)\}.$$

We equip $H$ with the edge-sum $L^2$ inner product and $V_D$ with

$$\|w\|_{V_D}^2=\sum_{e\in E}\int_0^{\ell_e}(|w_e|^2+|w'_e|^2)\,dx_e.$$

No Kirchhoff derivative condition is built into $V_D$; that condition is a
natural boundary condition of the later weak diffusion form. The elliptic
and P1 error results below assume that $D$ meets every connected edge
component.
def-conservative-network-advection-routi:
## Definition

At a directed network junction, let $n_{\rm in}$ edges carry nonnegative
incoming **mass fluxes** $q^{\rm in}_i$ into the junction, and let
$n_{\rm out}$ edges carry outgoing mass fluxes. A **conservative nonnegative
routing matrix** is a real matrix
$P\in\mathbb R^{n_{\rm out}\times n_{\rm in}}$ such that

$$P_{ji}\ge0,\qquad \sum_{j=1}^{n_{\rm out}}P_{ji}=1 \quad(1\le i\le n_{\rm in}).$$

It routes the incoming flux vector to
$q^{\rm out}=Pq^{\rm in}$. The column $i$ distributes the mass flux arriving
on incoming edge $i$ among the outgoing edges. The column-sum condition
stipulates no source or sink at the junction. It is a model condition on flux;
it does not assert that the densities on incident edges are equal.
def-finite-weighted-network-diffusion-da:
## Definition

Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph with ordered vertex and edge sets.
Choose an orientation of each edge and let $B\in\mathbb R^{V\times E}$ be
the resulting incidence matrix of
[[def-oriented-incidence-matrix-of-a-graph]]: a column has $-1$ at its tail,
$+1$ at its head, and zero elsewhere. Let $D\subseteq V$ be the vertices with
prescribed Dirichlet values and let $I=V\setminus D$ be the free vertices.
Assign a mass $m_i>0$ to each $i\in I$ and a conductance $c_e\ge0$ to each
$e\in E$. Put

$$M=\operatorname{diag}(m_i)_{i\in I},\qquad C=\operatorname{diag}(c_e)_{e\in E},\qquad L_C=BCB^{\mathsf T}.$$

The matrix $L_C$ is the **conductance-weighted graph stiffness**. Its free
Dirichlet restriction $L_D$ is the principal submatrix $(L_C)_{I,I}$. The
finite weighted network diffusion equation is

$$M u'(t)+L_Du(t)=f(t),$$

where $u(t)\in\mathbb R^I$ and $f(t)\in\mathbb R^I$. If $D=\varnothing$,
this is the closed Neumann network equation. If the boundary values are
instead a nonzero vector $g(t)$, restriction of $L_C(u,g)$ to $I$ gives
$M u'+L_Du=f-(L_C)_{I,D}g$.

When every $c_e=1$, $L_C=BB^{\mathsf T}$ agrees with the ordinary graph
Laplacian by
[[thm-laplacian-is-the-oriented-incidence-product]]. Zero conductances are
allowed and remove those edges from the diffusion coupling; they do not remove
the vertices or masses.
def-metric-graph-p1-edge-mesh:
## Definition

Assume $E\ne\varnothing$. For each edge $e$, choose a finite partition
$$0=x_{e,0}<x_{e,1}<\cdots<x_{e,N_e}=\ell_e,$$
where $N_e\ge1$, and let $\mathcal T_h$ be the union of the resulting
interval cells $K_{e,j}=[x_{e,j-1},x_{e,j}]$. Set
$h=\max_{e,j}(x_{e,j}-x_{e,j-1})$. The conforming **P1 edge space** is
$$V_h=\{w\in V_D:\ w_e\text{ is affine on every }K_{e,j}\}.$$
Thus internal nodal values are single-valued along each edge, while the
original-vertex matching and zero-anchor conditions are inherited from
$V_D$. The maximum step $h$ is positive and finite because the mesh has
finitely many cells of positive length.
lem-anchored-metric-graph-h1-space-is-hi:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a finite metric graph and anchor set $D$, the trace-matching space and
the anchored space $V_D$ of
[[def-anchored-finite-metric-graph-h1-space]] are closed real Hilbert
subspaces of $\bigoplus_{e\in E}H^1(0,\ell_e;\mathbb R)$ with the
edge-product $H^1$ inner product.
lem-anchored-metric-graph-poincare:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and assume every connected edge component of the finite metric graph $\Gamma$
has at least one anchor in $D$. Put
$L_\Gamma=\sum_{e\in E}\ell_e$. Then every $w\in V_D$ satisfies

$$\|w\|_{L^2(\Gamma)}\le L_\Gamma \left(\sum_{e\in E}\|w'_e\|_{L^2(e)}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
lem-metric-graph-kirchhoff-green-identit:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Orient each edge coordinate from $0$ at
$\partial_-e$ to $\ell_e$ at $\partial_+e$. For endpoint incidences
$(e,-)$ and $(e,+)$ define the outward derivatives by
$\partial_{\nu_{(e,-)}}u_e=-u'_e(0)$ and
$\partial_{\nu_{(e,+)}}u_e=+u'_e(\ell_e)$. The two incidences are both
included at a loop vertex. For $\iota=(e,\pm)$ write $e(\iota)=e$.
If $u_e\in H^2(0,\ell_e)$, with $H^2$ as defined by
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]],
$v\in V_D$, and each edge has a constant diffusivity $\kappa_e>0$, then

$$\sum_{e\in E}\kappa_e\int_0^{\ell_e}u'_ev'_e\,dx_e =-\sum_{e\in E}\kappa_e\int_0^{\ell_e}u''_ev_e\,dx_e +\sum_{z\in V}v(z)\sum_{\iota\in\mathcal I(z)}\kappa_{e(\iota)}\partial_{\nu_\iota}u_{e(\iota)}(z).$$

Thus zero test traces remove anchored endpoint terms, and a Kirchhoff
condition
$\sum_{\iota\in\mathcal I(z)}\kappa_{e(\iota)}\partial_{\nu_\iota}u_{e(\iota)}(z)=0$ at each free vertex
cancels the remaining terms.
lem-weighted-network-energy-kernel-and-m:
## Statement

Use the data of [[def-finite-weighted-network-diffusion-data]]. Let
$E_+=\{e\in E:c_e>0\}$ and let $G_+=(V,E_+)$; its connected components are
the **positive-conductance components**. For $x\in\mathbb R^I$, let
$\bar x\in\mathbb R^V$ equal $x$ on $I$ and $0$ on $D$. Then

$$x^{\mathsf T}L_Dx=\sum_{e\in E}c_e (\bar x_{\mathrm{head}(e)}-\bar x_{\mathrm{tail}(e)})^2\ge0.$$

Consequently $L_D$ is symmetric positive semidefinite, and $x\in\ker L_D$
exactly when $\bar x$ is constant on each positive-conductance component and
that constant is zero on every such component meeting $D$. In the closed
case $D=\varnothing$, every differentiable solution of
$Mu'+L_Cu=f$ satisfies

$$\frac{d}{dt}\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}Mu(t)=\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}f(t).$$

Thus homogeneous closed diffusion conserves weighted mass
$\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}Mu$, which need not equal the unweighted sum
$\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}u$.
thm-conservative-network-routing-conserv:
## Statement

Let $P$ be a conservative nonnegative routing matrix from
[[def-conservative-network-advection-routing]], and let
$q^{\rm in}\in\mathbb R^{n_{\rm in}}$ be entrywise nonnegative. Then
$q^{\rm out}=Pq^{\rm in}$ is entrywise nonnegative and
$$\sum_{j=1}^{n_{\rm out}}q^{\rm out}_j =\sum_{i=1}^{n_{\rm in}}q^{\rm in}_i.$$
cor-weighted-network-gauged-cg-applicabi:
## Statement

Use the weighted network data of
[[def-finite-weighted-network-diffusion-data]]. The exact-arithmetic
conjugate-gradient result
[[thm-conjugate-gradient-is-the-krylov-galerkin-method-and-minimizes-the-energy-error]]
applies to each of the following systems:

1. $M+\tau L_D$ for every $\tau>0$;
2. the grounded steady matrix $L_D$ if every positive-conductance component
   containing a free vertex also meets the Dirichlet set $D$;
3. the closed Neumann matrix $L_C$ restricted to $K^\perp$, where
   $K=\ker L_C$, for every compatible right-hand side $b\in K^\perp$.

In case 3 the gauge $u\in K^\perp$ gives the unique solution of $L_Cu=b$.
Here $K^\perp$ uses the standard Euclidean inner product
$\langle x,y\rangle=x^{\mathsf T}y$. If a stated unknown space is
zero-dimensional, its solver claim is vacuous.
These are exact-arithmetic applicability claims only; no finite-precision
stability claim is made.
lem-metric-graph-p1-interpolation-estima:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice, any anchor set $D\subseteq V$ as in
[[def-anchored-finite-metric-graph-h1-space]], a mesh
$\mathcal T_h$ of [[def-metric-graph-p1-edge-mesh]], positive constants
$\kappa_e$ on the edges, and edgewise $u_e\in H^2(0,\ell_e)$ as in
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], with the
trace matching and anchor conditions of $V_D$. Let $I_hu$ be the edgewise
nodal linear interpolant. Then $I_hu\in V_h$ and
$$\left(\sum_{e\in E}\kappa_e\|(u_e-I_hu_e)'\|_{L^2(e)}^2\right)^{1/2} \le h\left(\sum_{e\in E}\kappa_e\|u''_e\|_{L^2(e)}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
thm-metric-graph-p1-parabolic-semidiscre:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let a finite metric graph
with nonempty edge set have every connected edge component anchored, let
$V=V_D$ and $H=\bigoplus_{e\in E}L^2(0,\ell_e;\mathbb R)$, and let $V_h$
be its conforming P1 edge space. Put $L_\Gamma=\sum_e\ell_e$,
$\alpha=\kappa_{\min}/(1+L_\Gamma^2)$, and assume constant diffusivities
$0<\kappa_{\min}\le\kappa_e\le\kappa_{\max}$. For $T>0$,
$f\in L^2(0,T;V_D^*)$, and $u_h^0\in V_h$, define
$a(w,v)=\sum_e\kappa_e\int_0^{\ell_e}w'_ev'_e\,dx_e$. There is a unique
$u_h\in H^1(0,T;V_h)$ with $u_h(0)=u_h^0$ satisfying, for almost every $t$,

$$((u_h)'(t),v_h)_H+a(u_h(t),v_h)=\langle f(t),v_h\rangle_{V_D^*,V_D}\qquad(v_h\in V_h).$$

For every $t\in[0,T]$,

$$\|u_h(t)\|_H^2+\alpha\int_0^t\|u_h(s)\|_{V_D}^2\,ds\le\|u_h^0\|_H^2+\alpha^{-1}\int_0^t\|f(s)\|_{V_D^*}^2\,ds.$$

Here $V_h$ is the finite P1 space from
[[def-metric-graph-p1-edge-mesh]]. This is a semidiscrete
existence and energy statement; it gives no parabolic spatial error rate.
thm-metric-graph-weak-elliptic-problem:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice, $E\ne\varnothing$, and that the anchor set $D$ meets every connected
edge component of the finite metric graph $\Gamma$. Let constant edge
diffusivities satisfy
$$0<\kappa_{\min}\le\kappa_e\le\kappa_{\max}<\infty.$$
For every $f\in H=\bigoplus_{e\in E}L^2(0,\ell_e;\mathbb R)$ there is a unique
$u\in V_D$ such that

$$a(u,v):=\sum_{e\in E}\kappa_e\int_0^{\ell_e}u'_ev'_e\,dx_e=F(v):=\sum_{e\in E}\int_0^{\ell_e}f_ev_e\,dx_e\qquad(v\in V_D).$$

The equation is the anchored weak metric-graph diffusion problem. Whenever
$u_e\in H^2(0,\ell_e)$ as defined in
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], the Green identity
[[lem-metric-graph-kirchhoff-green-identity]] identifies its interior
equation as $-\kappa_eu''_e=f_e$ and its natural free-vertex condition as
Kirchhoff balance of the outward diffusive fluxes.
thm-weighted-network-semigroup-and-euler:
## Statement

Use the data of [[def-finite-weighted-network-diffusion-data]] and write
$L=L_D$. For any $t\ge0$, the homogeneous exact semigroup
$$S_D(t)=e^{-tM^{-1}L}$$
maps entrywise nonnegative initial vectors to entrywise nonnegative vectors.
For a forward Euler step of size $\tau\ge0$, the map
$$E_F(\tau)=I-\tau M^{-1}L$$
is entrywise nonnegative, and hence positivity preserving for every
nonnegative input, exactly when
$$0\le\tau\le\tau_F:=\min_{\substack{i\in I\\L_{ii}>0}}\frac{m_i}{L_{ii}},$$
where the minimum of an empty set is $+\infty$. For every $\tau>0$, the
backward Euler map $(M+\tau L)^{-1}M$ exists and is positivity preserving.
The forward Euler threshold is sharp for positivity of the full step matrix.
thm-metric-graph-p1-fem-cea-and-energy-r:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice, every edge component is anchored, each $\kappa_e$ is constant with
$0<\kappa_{\min}\le\kappa_e\le\kappa_{\max}$, and the weak solution $u$ of
[[thm-metric-graph-weak-elliptic-problem]] satisfies
$u_e\in H^2(0,\ell_e)$, as defined in
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], on every edge. For the conforming P1 space $V_h$ of
[[def-metric-graph-p1-edge-mesh]], let $u_h\in V_h$ solve
$$a(u_h,v_h)=F(v_h)\qquad(v_h\in V_h),$$
where $a$ and $F$ are the weak diffusion form and load of that theorem. Put
$L_\Gamma=\sum_e\ell_e$,
$M_a=\kappa_{\max}$, and
$\alpha_a=\kappa_{\min}/(1+L_\Gamma^2)$. Then $u_h$ exists uniquely and
$$\|u-u_h\|_{V_D}\le\frac{M_a}{\alpha_a}\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\|u-v_h\|_{V_D}.$$
$$\left(\sum_e\kappa_e\|(u_e-u_{h,e})'\|_{L^2(e)}^2\right)^{1/2}\le h\left(\sum_e\kappa_e\|u''_e\|_{L^2(e)}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
Thus the energy-seminorm error is $O(h)$ for this fixed finite graph and
edgewise H2 solution. The Green identity
[[lem-metric-graph-kirchhoff-green-identity]] identifies the natural
free-vertex condition as Kirchhoff balance; this theorem makes no claim for
vertex singularities or higher-dimensional junctions.
